question: What is tension in fly casting and why does it matter?
answer: Tension in fly casting refers to the degree of tautness maintained in the fly line throughout the cast and the drift. Understanding constant tension, increasing tension, and decreasing tension gives the caster control over every specialty cast — from pile casts that build slack into the presentation to tight line Euro nymphing that eliminates all slack. The same principle applies equally on small Smoky Mountain streams and 30-knot saltwater flats.
